header.running_head: The Noble Character of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.text: companions or family called for him, he always responded by saying, 'At your service.' It was for this reason that Allaah revealed the verse:
Verily, you (O Rasulullaah ﷺ) are (firmly stationed) upon an exalted (flawless) character.

Hadhrat Qais bin Wahab reports from a man from the Banu Suraat tribe that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Tell me about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Have you not read in the Qur'aan where Allaah says:?" She then continued, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was once with his companions when I and Hafsah (RA) both prepared some food for him. When she beat me to sending the food, I sent my slave girl with instructions to overturn the platter. Consequently, when Hafsah (RA) was serving the food to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the slave girl overturned it and the food was all scattered about. Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered the food that had fallen on the ground and the Sahabah (RA) ate it. When I sent my platter, Rasulullaah ﷺ handed it over to Hafsah (RA) saying, 'Take this platter in place of yours and eat whatever is in it.' I did not notice even a hint of displeasure on the face of Rasulullaah ﷺ."[^2]
The statement of Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid narrates that a group of people once came to his father Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) with the request, "Tell us something about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) said, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's neighbour. When revelation would come to him, he would send for me and I would come to him to write it down. Whenever we spoke of worldly matters, he also spoke about it, whenever we spoke of the Aakhirah, he also spoke about it and whenever we spoke of food, he also spoke of the same (he was never aloof from us). I am narrating all this to you on behalf of Rasulullaah ﷺ."[^3]

Hadhrat Safiyya bint Huyay (RA) (Rasulullaah ﷺ's wife) says, "I have never seen anyone with better character than Rasulullaah ﷺ. I was riding on the back of his camel with him as we returned from Khaybar. It was at night and as I began to fall asleep, my head hit the back of the carriage. Rasulullaah ﷺ touched me gently as he said, 'Take it easy, dear lady. Take it easy, O daughter of Huyay (this is not the place to sleep).' When we reached a place called Sahbaa, he said to me,
Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.44).

Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.57). Tirmidhi and Bayhaqi have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.42) as has Tabraani as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.17). Ibn Abu Dawood in his Masaahif, Abu Ya'la, Rooyaani and Ibn Asaakir have also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.185). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.90) has reported a similar narration as well.
